To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) policymakers should condition a policy instrument on information when it is used by agents to learn, and (ii) policymakers should disclose information when it is useful for agents to use in a competitive environment.

(a) the optimal policy instrument or disclosure will be used to address the same underlying problem; (b) the optimal instrument will be used in economies where information has a large effect on welfare and where the policymaker has little information; and (c) disclosure will be optimal in economies where information is less important, where the policymaker is more informed, and where the policymarker’s information is less costly to use

(1) disclosure is desirable in a broad class of economies; (2) in a class of economies with dispersed information, learning, and payoff externalities, the use of a policy tool is desirable; and (3) in economies that are not characterized by these three properties, the use of disclosure or a policy tool is not necessarily optimal.
